cards.narrative: Central Texas is getting a space-age industrial boom, but it's not just about rockets — it's about who profits and who gets the jobs.
cards.paragraph: Blue Origin wants to drop a 1.3 million square foot plant in Hutto, a town that's about to become a space hub. The price tag: $650 million, which is a lot of football fields. This is Bezos betting big on Texas, and it's going to change Hutto's skyline and its tax base. But here's the thing — when a giant like that rolls in, the little guy gets squeezed. Housing costs go up, traffic gets worse, and the jobs might not go to locals. It's a classic Texas story: big money, big promises, and the people who live there wondering if they'll be left behind.
cards.data_point: The proposed Project Blue Hub plant will be about the size of 26 football fields – 1.3 million square feet at a cost of $650 million.

cards.narrative: Marina Mabrey's 53-point night is a reminder that the WNBA's new stars are rewriting the record books — and getting paid for it.
cards.paragraph: Marina Mabrey tied the WNBA single-game scoring record with 53 points, and she did it in Toronto, a city that just got a team. The front office locked her up with a $2.4 million deal, which is a big number for a league that's still fighting for respect. But here's the thing: Mabrey isn't just a scorer, she's a symbol. The WNBA's expansion is bringing new talent and new money, and players like her are proving they deserve every cent. It's not just about the points — it's about the power shift.
cards.data_point: Marina Mabrey tied the all-time WNBA single-game scoring record with 53 points.

cards.narrative: Basketball Without Borders is quietly doing the most important work at All-Star weekend, but it's not getting the headlines.
cards.paragraph: While everyone was talking about the All-Star game, 40 high-school-age players from around the world were at the Advocate Center, getting coached and mentored. This is where the next generation of basketball stars comes from, and it's a reminder that the game is global. The WNBA's growth isn't just about the pros — it's about the pipeline. These kids are the future, and programs like this are how the league builds its global brand. It's easy to forget, but this is the real story.
cards.data_point: 40 of the world's top high-school-age players participated in Basketball Without Borders at the Advocate Center.

cards.narrative: The WNBA's dildo-throwing problem is back, and it's a sign that the league's culture war is far from over.
cards.paragraph: A fan threw a dildo on the court during a Dream-Sparks game, and they got arrested and banned. This was supposed to be a 2025 problem, but here we are in 2026. The WNBA is dealing with a new culture war, and this incident shows it's not going away. It's not just about the object — it's about the disrespect. Players are trying to build a professional league, and they're dealing with this nonsense. The league needs to crack down hard, because this isn't just a prank, it's a attack on the game.
cards.data_point: A green dildo landed on the hardwood during the third quarter of the Dream-Sparks game.

cards.narrative: Kaitlyn Chen's rise from Princeton to the Valkyries is a reminder that the WNBA's new teams are finding gems in unexpected places.
cards.paragraph: Kaitlyn Chen wasn't a top pick, but she's putting the league on notice with Golden State. Her path went through Princeton, where she averaged 14.2 points a game, but she's proving that stats don't tell the whole story. The Valkyries took a chance on her, and she's paying it off. This is what expansion does — it gives overlooked players a shot, and it makes the league better. Chen's story is about more than basketball; it's about opportunity.
cards.data_point: Kaitlyn Chen averaged 14.2 points, 3.9 assists, 3.5 rebounds, and 1.1 steals at Princeton.

cards.narrative: Matt Campbell's 'truth bomb' about Penn State's expectations is a classic coach-speak that reveals the pressure cooker of big-time college football.
cards.paragraph: Matt Campbell told Pat McAfee that he looks at the lights on Beaver Stadium and thinks about the expectations. It's a soundbite, but it's also a window into the stress of taking over a program like Penn State. The fans want a national title, and Campbell knows it. He's not shying away from the pressure, but he's also managing it. This is the reality of college football's power structure — the coach is the one who has to deliver, or he's out.
cards.data_point: Matt Campbell described seeing Beaver Stadium late at night with the lights shining over the ongoing expansion.

cards.narrative: Minnesota suing Abbott to extradite an ICE agent is a state-vs-state fight that's really about federal power and immigration policy.
cards.paragraph: Minnesota is trying to force Texas to hand over an ICE agent accused of shooting a Venezuelan man. Abbott is refusing, and that's a direct challenge to the rule of law. This isn't just a legal dispute — it's a political statement. Abbott is positioning himself as the defender of immigration enforcement, even if it means defying another state. The question is: who wins? And what does it mean for the guy who got shot? This is about power, and it's messy.
cards.data_point: Minnesota sued Gov. Greg Abbott to force the extradition of an ICE agent accused of shooting a Venezuelan man.

cards.narrative: The $9.25 million defamation verdict against the New York Times is a warning to media: get the facts right, or pay the price.
cards.paragraph: A jury hit the Times with a $9.25 million verdict for falsely identifying Kai Spears in a shooting story. That's a big number, and it's a reminder that journalism has consequences. The Times made a mistake, and it cost them. This is about accountability — the media has power, and when they misuse it, they should be held responsible. Spears wasn't just a name in a story; he was a person whose life got turned upside down. This verdict is a win for the little guy.
cards.data_point: Kai Spears was awarded $9.25 million by a Tuscaloosa jury in a defamation lawsuit against the New York Times.

cards.narrative: The hemp industry's new lawsuit over Texas's THC ban is a David-vs-Goliath fight for the right to sell a legal product.
cards.paragraph: Texas banned THC, and now the hemp industry is fighting back, claiming job losses and a monopoly for medical marijuana. This is a classic regulatory battle: the state says one thing, but the industry says it's overreach. The lawsuit is about more than just THC — it's about who gets to control a lucrative market. Small businesses are at stake, and they're not going down without a fight. This could set a precedent for other states.
cards.data_point: The hemp industry filed a new lawsuit over Texas's THC ban, claiming job losses and a medical marijuana monopoly.

cards.narrative: Quality Control CEO Pierre 'P' Thomas's hospitalization is a stark reminder that even music moguls are mortal.
cards.paragraph: P Thomas is alive, but he's in the hospital, and the company had to put out a statement to clarify that. This is a scary moment for the hip-hop world, especially after HYBE bought his label for $300 million in 2023. Thomas built an empire, but health doesn't care about your net worth. The music industry is watching, and it's a reminder that behind the hits and the money, there's a human being.
cards.data_point: HYBE acquired QC Media Holdings for $300 million in 2023.

cards.narrative: Megan DiLeo's journey in Portland is a story of growth, not just in stats, but in resilience.
cards.paragraph: The Portland Fire are back in the WNBA after 24 years, and Megan DiLeo is part of that new chapter. They're 11-18, but that's not the point. DiLeo is developing, and the team is building something. This is what expansion is about — giving players a chance to grow and cities a reason to cheer. It's not always pretty, but it's real.
cards.data_point: The Portland Fire sit with an 11-18 record in their first season back in the WNBA.

cards.narrative: Google's SCIN dataset is a step toward making dermatology AI more equitable, but it's still early days.
cards.paragraph: SCIN is a new dataset that aims to represent the real world better, with a focus on early-stage skin conditions. That's important because most AI training data is skewed. But here's the catch: more than half the images are from less than a week before the photo, so it's still not fully representative. It's a start, but we need to be careful not to overhype it. The goal is to make healthcare AI work for everyone, not just the lucky few.
cards.data_point: More than half of SCIN images show early-stage concerns that arose less than a week before the photo.

cards.narrative: The Valkyries' win over the Lynx is a statement that they're not just a feel-good story — they're contenders.
cards.paragraph: Golden State finally beat Minnesota, and it matters. The Valkyries are hosting the All-Star Game in 2027, and they want a championship banner to go with it. This win shows they can hang with the best. It's a sign that the expansion teams aren't just there to make up the numbers — they're coming for the title. The WNBA is getting more competitive, and that's good for everyone.
cards.data_point: The Valkyries hosted WNBA All-Star 2027 and are chasing a championship banner.

cards.narrative: Young players like Makayla Timpson are proving that the WNBA's future is in good hands, even if they're not the headliners.
cards.paragraph: Everyone talks about the big stars, but it's the role players who often make the difference. Timpson fits perfectly with the Fever, and similar players are elevating the Valkyries and Liberty. These are the unsung heroes of the playoff push. They don't get the headlines, but they're the ones doing the dirty work. That's what makes a championship team.
cards.data_point: Makayla Timpson has turned out to be the perfect fit next to the Indiana Fever's star players.
